report.incident_title: Search results missing products / some searches fail
report.summary: Confirmed by logs and infra events: es-data-3 failed on hardware at 15:17Z (E3, E19). The es-products cluster went HealthRed at 15:18:30Z with two primary shards of the products index unassigned and no replicas available (E4, E18). Data-node count dropped from 3 to 2 and unassigned shards rose to 2 between the 15:20 and 15:30 metric samples (E13). search-svc then logged partial results at 15:19:02Z (2 of 10 shards failed, NoShardAvailableActionException) and a failed brand-filtered query at 15:21:40Z (E1, E2). This matches the reported missing brands and failed searches. The 09-16 change record says products was reindexed with number_of_replicas=0 as a cost saving, with replicas to be re-enabled after verification and follow-up SRCH-311 still open (E20). That setting was not directly verified via an index settings API or logs (E10, E12, E14), so it is treated as recorded, not observed. The web-frontend v12.3.0 deploy at 15:00Z is not supported as the cause: the errors are shard-availability failures, no search-svc change was recorded, and the deploy came 17 minutes before the node failure with no evidence it altered requests (E1, E2, E22, E23). The prometheus relabel at 12:55Z has no described path to search request handling (E24). No metrics cover the 15:00-16:00Z window and no error traces were returned, so failure rates and the missing-brand scope are not quantified (E6, E7, E17). Why es-data-3 failed, and whether the two primaries are still unassigned or recoverable, remain unverified.
report.root_cause: Elasticsearch index products (10 primary shards, es-products cluster) was reindexed on 2026-09-16 with number_of_replicas=0 per change record (E20). When data node es-data-3 failed on hardware at 15:17Z (E3, E19), the two primary shards it held had no replica copies to promote. They became unassigned, and the cluster went HealthRed at 15:18:30Z (E4, E18). search-svc queries that fan out to all 10 shards then received partial results (2 of 10 shards failed) and, for brand-filtered queries routed to the unavailable shards, failed outright (E1, E2). This explains the missing brands and failed searches from about 15:20. The replicas=0 setting is per the change record and is not independently verified via index settings.

hypotheses.statement: es-products was reindexed on 2026-09-16 with number_of_replicas=0, so its primary shards have no replicas; a node loss or restart around 15:20 left some shards unassigned, so search-svc queries return partial results (missing brands) and fail when the required shards are unavailable.

facts.text: search-svc WARN at 15:19:02Z: 'partial results: 2 of 10 shards failed (NoShardAvailableActionException) index=products'. This is a shard-availability failure, not a malformed-parameter error.

search-svc ERROR at 15:21:40Z: 'search failed: all shards failed for filtered query (brand filter routed to unavailable shards)'. The failure is tied to brand-filter routing to unavailable shards, which matches missing brands and failed searches.
Infra event at 15:17:00Z (aws-ec2, instance/es-data-3): 'Instance status check failed (hardware); instance unreachable'.

Elasticsearch event at 15:18:30Z (cluster/es-products, HealthRed): 'node es-data-3 left; 2 primary shards of [products] unassigned (no replicas available)'. This shows the primaries had no replica copies to fail over to, which is the mechanism H2 proposes. It precedes the first search-svc shard failure at 15:19:02Z.

es-products data_nodes dropped from 3.0 (sampled 15:20Z) to 2.0 (sampled 15:30Z) and unassigned_shards rose from 0 to 2.0 at the 15:30Z sample and stayed at 2 through 16:00Z. The node loss occurred between the 15:20 and 15:30 samples, matching the reported ~15:20 onset.

Two unassigned shards with one data node lost is consistent with primaries that have no replica copies (replicas=0), so a node loss leaves those shards unassigned. This is an inference; replica settings were not directly observed.
es-products cluster went HealthRed at 2026-09-23T15:18:30Z: 'node es-data-3 left; 2 primary shards of [products] unassigned (no replicas available)'.
AWS EC2 reported instance/es-data-3 'Instance status check failed (hardware); instance unreachable' at 2026-09-23T15:17:00Z, about 1.5 minutes before the cluster HealthRed event.

Change record: es-products config change on 2026-09-16T11:00Z, 'Reindex products into new cluster with number_of_replicas=0 (cost saving)', author search-team; details say replicas were to be re-enabled after verification and follow-up ticket SRCH-311 is still open.

The v12.3.0 deploy (15:00Z) precedes the es-data-3 failure (15:17Z) and cluster HealthRed (15:18:30Z) by 17-18 minutes; the deploy is not the only event before the failure, and the record offers no evidence that the deploy altered search requests.
No search-svc changes recorded from 2026-09-10 to the window end (empty result).

No error traces touching es-products between 15:00 and 16:00Z on 2026-09-23 (empty result), which is inconsistent with search failures being reported at es-products level; either traces are not captured for this path or failures are returned upstream in search-svc.

corrective_actions.action: Restore the two unassigned products primary shards: recover or replace es-data-3 so the shards can be reallocated, or restore the affected shards from the most recent snapshot if the local copies are lost. Confirm cluster health returns to green and search-svc stops logging NoShardAvailableActionException.
corrective_actions.rationale: The user-facing failures continue while two primaries are unassigned (E4, E13, E1, E2). Restoring shard availability addresses the immediate impact. Whether the data on es-data-3 is recoverable is unknown and must be checked first.

corrective_actions.action: Verify the current number_of_replicas setting on products through the ES settings API, then set it to at least 1 and let replicas allocate. Close or act on SRCH-311.
corrective_actions.rationale: The replicas=0 setting is the condition that turned a single node loss into unassigned primaries (E20, E14). Enabling replicas removes this single point of failure. Verification first avoids acting on an unconfirmed setting.

corrective_actions.action: Add a change-review check that blocks production indices from being created or reindexed with number_of_replicas=0, and require a documented replica-restoration date for any temporary exception.
corrective_actions.rationale: The cost-saving change was made with replica restoration deferred to a follow-up ticket that remained open, so the risk was carried silently (E20). A review gate stops recurrence.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on es-products cluster status not green, unassigned shard count above zero, and data-node count dropping, and alert on search-svc partial_results_rate by index. Make sure metrics for the search path are retained and queryable for incident windows.
corrective_actions.rationale: No alert fired for the 09-16 to 09-23 16:00Z period, including around the node loss (E15). Metric and trace gaps also prevented quantifying the impact (E6, E7, E8).
